title: Romesco Paella-Stuffed Tomatoes with Bravas-Style Jersey Royals
description: Large tomatoes stuffed with warmed vegetarian paella, feta and romesco, served with crispy baby Jersey Royals, roasted red pepper, red onion and garlic in a smoky-sweet romesco-bravas-style sauce. Finished with black garlic aioli and fresh basil. A one-jar leftover upgrade — V1 Final.

servings.note: today, with easy repeat for 2 more tomorrow

items.name: Large tomatoes, hollowed (keep flesh and juices for sauce)
Leftover vegetarian paella, enough to fill the tomatoes
Dried oregano, thyme or mixed dried Italian herbs
Sliced garlic flakes (half the batch below), or to taste
Mixed dried Italian herbs, small pinch
Piri salt, tiny amount, only if needed
Baby Jersey Royals, cut to 2.5-3cm pieces
Red pepper, medium-thin lengthways slices cut into 3-5cm lengths
Red onion, cut as a flower, kept together for slow roasting
Whole garlic cloves, skin on if possible
Remaining sliced garlic flakes (other half of the batch above)
Chilli flakes, small pinch, added part-way through

steps.title: Make and reduce the sauce
steps.body: Warm the olive oil and butter gently. Add the tomato flesh and juices, half the garlic flakes, garlic powder, dried herbs, chilli flakes and black pepper. Cook covered for 5-8 minutes to soften, then add the romesco and cider vinegar. Continue low and slow until the colour deepens, breaking down larger pieces with a spoon or masher. Finish with the lid ajar or uncovered until spoonable rather than watery.

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.body: Preheat the oven. Toss the Jersey Royals with olive oil, garlic powder, dried herbs, black pepper and a very small amount of piri salt. Spread in one layer, preferably cut-side down. Add the red onion flower and whole garlic cloves. Roast for 12-15 minutes.

steps.title: Add red pepper
steps.body: Add the shortened red pepper strips after 12-15 minutes. This lets them soften and become part of the potatoes without collapsing too far. Keep the onion flower mostly intact.

steps.title: Add garlic flakes and chilli
steps.body: At around 22-25 minutes, add the remaining sliced garlic flakes and a small pinch of chilli flakes. If the garlic is very thin, add it for only the final 5-8 minutes. Aim for golden, not dark brown.

steps.title: Warm the paella for today only
steps.body: Warm only enough paella for the tomatoes you are eating today. Heat with a spoonful of romesco or sauce, or a tiny splash of water, until steaming and piping hot. Do not warm the portion you plan to use tomorrow.

steps.title: Stuff the tomatoes
steps.body: Mix the hot paella with 1-2 tbsp romesco, a spoonful of sauce if it needs moisture, some feta, black pepper and a pinch of dried herbs. Fill the tomato shells without packing too tightly. Top with feta, a tiny drizzle of olive oil and black pepper.

steps.title: Sauce-glaze the potatoes
steps.body: When the potatoes are nearly cooked, spoon over some romesco-bravas sauce and toss lightly so it coats the potatoes, peppers and roasted onion. Return to the oven for 5-7 minutes. Keep some sauce back for serving.

steps.title: Bake the stuffed tomatoes
steps.body: Reduce the oven to 180°C fan. Put the tomatoes in a small dish with a spoonful of sauce around the base, but do not flood them. Bake for 15-20 minutes if filled with hot paella. They are ready when softened, the feta has caught slightly and the filling is piping hot in the centre.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.body: Spoon reserved sauce onto the plate. Add stuffed tomatoes and bravas-style potatoes. Finish with black garlic aioli, torn fresh basil, optional extra feta and black pepper.

notes.label: Kitchen notes
notes.body: Skip breadcrumbs — the potatoes provide crisp texture and feta gives salt and creaminess. Keep the sauce rustic: reduce and crush rather than fully blend. Cut the red pepper shorter so it integrates into the potato tray rather than becoming a separate side. Main jar opened: Romesco only.

notes.label: Storage & leftovers
notes.body: Because the filling contains leftover rice, reheat only the portion you are eating and make sure it is piping hot before stuffing. Keep tomorrow's paella portion cold in the fridge and reheat it tomorrow only once, until piping hot. Store any extra sauce covered in the fridge and reheat gently. Hollowed tomato shells can be stored separately, covered and upside down on kitchen paper, then stuffed tomorrow.

notes.label: Flavour profile
notes.body: Smoky-sweet from romesco, pepper and roasted onion; savoury from garlic and black garlic aioli; lightly sharp from cider vinegar and tomato; salty-creamy from feta; fresh from basil; and gently warm from piri salt and chilli rather than aggressively spicy.
